title: Tottenham Commercial & Sponsor Usage — Demo
source: FICTIONAL. Written by the REROUTE team for the hackathon demo as an alternative to the social media package: the club's commercial and partnership terms for sponsored and sales posts (partner activations incl. a sleeve partner, a home-market retail window, no broadcast footage in paid or sales content). No Tottenham Hotspur, Premier League, player or sponsor agreement was supplied or consulted.
disclaimer: FICTIONAL DEMO POLICY — not an actual club, league, player or sponsor agreement. DEMO POLICY — NOT VERIFIED LEGAL CLEARANCE.

provenance.description: Club-produced footage filed in the club's ScorePlay workspace and tagged "partner content"

rules.explanation: Premier League 2026/27 footage is covered by the club's commercial licence.
Allowed only on the club's own Instagram, Facebook, X, TikTok and YouTube accounts.
Editorial and organic club posts are licensed for GB, IE, US, CA, AU and NZ.
Sponsored partner posts are licensed for GB, IE and US — the markets where the partner deals are active.
Sales posts (shirts, tickets, memberships) are licensed for GB and IE only.
Sales posts can't run outside the UK and Ireland (GB, IE) — retail rights abroad belong to regional licensees.
Full-match recordings can only be shown in the UK and Ireland (GB, IE) — they come from the live broadcast feed.
Allowed for editorial, organic, sponsored and sales posts, as long as the market, people and brand rules are met.
Broadcast highlights and full matches can't be used in sponsored or sales posts — use club-produced footage instead.
The licence runs for the 2026/27 season: 1 Jul 2026 to 30 Jun 2027.
Players, staff and fans in match-day footage can appear in editorial and organic club posts.
Sponsored and sales posts can show Tottenham's own first-team squad and staff — only if ScorePlay lists them in the squad.
Crowd and stadium shots can be used in sponsored and sales posts (stadium conditions of entry) when no player is identifiable.
Kit branding and stadium boards that appear incidentally are fine in editorial and organic posts.
Sponsored and sales posts can show the club's own marks, main partner AIA, kit partner Nike and sleeve partner Kraken.
Sponsored and sales posts can't show any other brand or another club's crest — the club's partners have exclusivity.
